name: Amaethon

attributes.attribute: tends the deer and the lapwing

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Amaethon is a Welsh god. His name means plowman. He was a spirit of the fertile earth, tied to the harvest. Yet his care reached past the plowed field. He also tended the dog, the deer, and the lapwing. In the Welsh Triads, he had these three from the king of the Underworld. Their theft from the Otherworld shows that the plenty of this land comes from the far realm. Amaethon is a son of the mother goddess Dôn. He appears as a farmer in the tale of the Boar's yoke, able to make the most useless waste flower.
objective: Record Amaethon, the Welsh plowman god.
